hallucinations.claim: "The NVIDIA Blackwell B100 is the most powerful GPU for general AI workloads right now"
hallucinations.why: As of Oct 2026 the top shipping accelerator is Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300 NVL72), with Vera Rubin in first customer shipments; the B100 is a superseded 2024 part that barely shipped in volume.

hallucinations.claim: "Claude 3.5 Sonnet runs exclusively on Google Cloud's Ironwood TPUs"
hallucinations.why: Trap: Anthropic trains and serves on AWS Trainium (primary training partner, 1M+ Trainium2), Google TPUs and Nvidia GPUs; never 'exclusively' TPUs. Claude 3.5 Sonnet is also a 2024 model, not current.

hallucinations.claim: "Ironwood TPUs (fifth-gen TPU v5)" / "the current flagship is Ironwood (v5)"
hallucinations.why: Ironwood is TPU v7 (TPU7x); v5e/v5p are 2023 parts.

hallucinations.claim: "TPU v6 does not exist yet"
hallucinations.why: TPU v6 (Trillium) shipped in 2024; Ironwood (v7) is GA since April 2026 and TPU 8t/8i were announced April 2026.

hallucinations.claim: "Anthropic's $30B compute deal with Broadcom/Google Cloud in April 2026"
hallucinations.why: Source [8] (spoonai) headline is '$30B Revenue' plus a compute deal; the $30B figure is revenue, not the deal size. Misattributed number.

hallucinations.claim: "locked them into Google's TPU pods for inference"
hallucinations.why: Anthropic is multi-platform (Trainium, TPU, Nvidia) and signed an April 2026 Amazon deal for up to 5 GW; not locked in.

hallucinations.claim: "Google's Pathways runtime and BF16 precision giving it a speed advantage for sparse workloads like LLM inference"
hallucinations.why: Unsourced technical claim about Claude's serving stack; nothing in the packet supports Anthropic using Pathways, and LLM inference is not a 'sparse workload' in this sense.

hallucinations.claim: "Groq LPU-96K"
hallucinations.why: No such Groq product name; invented.

hallucinations.claim: "sub-10ms latency inference" for Groq
hallucinations.why: Unverifiable specific attributed to a comparison blog.

hallucinations.claim: "Cerebras WSE-3 — wafer-scale chip (270TB DRAM)"
hallucinations.why: WSE-3 has ~44 GB of on-chip SRAM, not 270 TB of DRAM.

hallucinations.claim: Graphcore IPU listed among the dominant specialized architectures
hallucinations.why: Graphcore was acquired by SoftBank in 2024 and is not a current AI-leader platform; stale.

hallucinations.claim: "Google's open-source Gemma 3 is optimized for Nvidia GPUs" offered as what Google uses
hallucinations.why: Gemma 3 is a March 2025 open model; Google trains Gemini on its own TPUs. Off-point and stale.

hallucinations.claim: "Meta and Mistral also run on Nvidia's Blackwell/Hopper" (only)
hallucinations.why: Meta also runs AMD (6 GW MI450 deal) and its own MTIA; incomplete picture presented as the answer.

what_went_wrong: Search returned generic 2026 'GPU vs TPU' blogs and an old Decrypt piece, none on Blackwell Ultra, Vera Rubin, MI450 or Trainium; all three drafts fell back on stale model memory (B100, 'TPU v6 pod') and the ministral merge invented specs (270TB DRAM, LPU-96K) and the TPU-only Claude claim.
great_answer_would: Say 'as of October 2026: Blackwell Ultra B300/GB300 shipping, Vera Rubin ramping; Ironwood TPU v7 GA with TPU 8 announced; MI355X shipping, MI450 Helios in H2 2026', then Claude on Trainium + TPUs + Nvidia, and one line each for OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI.
notes: OpenAI on Nvidia Blackwell/Hopper is roughly right but misses AMD MI450 and Broadcom. No mention of AMD, Trainium, Vera Rubin or xAI. No 'changed recently' flag despite the asker's preference. The B100-as-top claim is the central fact and is wrong, capping correct_current.
